title: Phylogeographic epidemiology of Dabie bandavirus in East Asia: divergent transmission networks and genotype‐linked clinical severity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to elucidate the distinct ecological drivers and phylogeographic dynamics underlying the geographically decoupled incidence and fatality patterns of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) across East Asia. SFTS, caused by Dabie bandavirus (SFTSV), exhibits varying incidence and fatality rates in inland and coastal regions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study integrated 1820 high-quality global genomes of SFTSV with clinical cohorts (936 patients) and nationwide surveillance data (27,457 cases) from China, employing ecological modeling, Bayesian phylogeography, and genotype-phenotype association analyses.
analysis.methods: Ecological modeling, Bayesian phylogeography, and genotype-phenotype association analyses were used to trace the evolutionary trajectories and clinical implications of SFTSV. The study utilized well-characterized clinical cohorts and nationwide surveillance data from China.
analysis.main_results: A pronounced 'inland-high-incidence vs. coastal-high-fatality' pattern of SFTS was identified. The incidence of SFTS exhibited divergent sensitivities to meteorological factors, with inland transmission being sensitive to thermal fluctuations and coastal dynamics constrained by a sunshine threshold (> 200 h/month). Spatial divergence in clinical severity correlated with the distribution of regional viral genetic structures, with inland regions mainly co-circulating genotypes A, C, and D, and coastal regions dominated by genotype B. Zhejiang province was identified as a genetic hub with significantly higher recombination frequencies than inland regions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that risk assessment must extend beyond incidence alone and provide a phylogeographically informed framework for targeted surveillance and genotype-specific interventions in high-risk hotspots. The study identified divergent meteorological factors and plausible maritime transmission networks underlying the geographically decoupled epidemiology of SFTS.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform targeted surveillance and genotype-specific interventions in high-risk hotspots, enhancing the understanding of SFTS epidemiology and contributing to improved public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design limitations include the reliance on surveillance data and the potential for sampling bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and the need for further functional validation of the molecular correlates of fatal outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study elucidated the distinct ecological drivers and phylogeographic dynamics of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in East Asia, identifying divergent meteorological factors and genetic structures underlying the geographically decoupled incidence and fatality patterns. The findings highlight the need for targeted surveillance and genotype-specific interventions.

title: Evaluation of new adjuvants in enhancing the immune response to a candidate of Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus vaccine.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Here, we evaluated a beta-propiolactone-inactivated SFTSV vaccine candidate based on strain YL1, formulated with benchmark adjuvants (Addavax and Alhydrogel) or experimental innate immune agonists, including Sendai virus-derived defective interfering RNA (SDI), a RIG-I agonist, and imidazoquinoline-poly(ethylene glycol)-cholesterol conjugate (IMDQ-P-C), a TLR7/8 agonist, alone or in combination.
analysis.study_design_and_population: SFTSV is primarily transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicorn is ticks and can cause a hemorrhagic fever-like illness characterized by high fever, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and multiorgan failure, with reported case-fatality rates ranging from 10% to over 30%.
analysis.methods: Using an extended prime-boost regimen, we examined adjuvant-dependent modulation of humoral immunity, antigen-specific cellular recall, antibody cross-reactivity, and functional protection following passive serum transfer and live-virus challenge in IFNAR-/- mice.
analysis.main_results: NP-induced recall showed mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across vaccine formulations, whereas the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited humoral and cellular responses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Together, these findings support the immunogenicity and protective potential of a BPL-inactivated SFTSV vaccine platform and identify NP as a major target of vaccine-induced immune memory.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Despite its growing public health relevance, no licensed vaccines or specific antiviral therapies are currently available.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Sera from Addavax- and SDI-adjuvanted groups displayed cross-reactivity with the Gn glycoprotein of the heterologous HB29 strain and conferred partial protection following passive transfer into IFNAR-/- mice challenged with live SFTSV.

analysis.summary_en: Here, we evaluated a beta-propiolactone-inactivated SFTSV vaccine candidate based on strain YL1, formulated with benchmark adjuvants (Addavax and Alhydrogel) or experimental innate immune agonists, including Sendai virus-derived defective interfering RNA (SDI), a RIG-I agonist, and imidazoquinoline-poly(ethylene glycol)-cholesterol conjugate (IMDQ-P-C), a TLR7/8 agonist, alone or in combination. SFTSV is primarily transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicorn is ticks and can cause a hemorrhagic fever-like illness characterized by high fever, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and multiorgan failure, with reported case-fatality rates ranging from 10% to over 30%. Using an extended prime-boost regimen, we examined adjuvant-dependent modulation of humoral immunity, antigen-specific cellular recall, antibody cross-reactivity, and functional protection following passive serum transfer and live-virus challenge in IFNAR-/- mice. NP-induced recall showed mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across vaccine formulations, whereas the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited humoral and cellular responses. Together, these findings support the immunogenicity and protective potential of a BPL-inactivated SFTSV vaccine platform and identify NP as a major target of vaccine-induced immune memory. Despite its growing public health relevance, no licensed vaccines or specific antiviral therapies are currently available. Sera from Addavax- and SDI-adjuvanted groups displayed cross-reactivity with the Gn glycoprotein of the heterologous HB29 strain and conferred partial protection following passive transfer into IFNAR-/- mice challenged with live SFTSV.

analysis.summary_en: Whether a common mechanism exists that promotes virus-triggered mitochondria-derived inflammation is currently unknown. The supplied evidence does not clearly state the study design, setting, or study population. Using the Bak-/- mouse model, we showed that both IAV and SFTSV, two viruses that induce severe inflammation in patients, trigger BAK up-regulation and BAK-dependent lethal inflammation. Viral infection triggers STAT1-dependent up-regulation of IRF1, which binds to an identified ISRE site in the BAK-promoter, inducing BAK up-regulation. Both RNA and DNA viruses trigger the IRF1-mediated BAK up-regulation and mitochondria-derived inflammation. These results reveal a common mechanism that drives mitochondria-derived pathogenic inflammation, which can be targeted for developing anti-inflammatory therapeutics. Up-regulated BAK accumulates in the mitochondria triggering mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization and inflammatory responses.
